title: SSE telemetry enrichment and customer retry playbook for midstream disconnects and partial output merges
creator: Daniel Mercer
description: High-severity customer escalations reported partial or truncated streaming responses over Hosted SSE. On reconnects customers saw either duplicated tokens, missing final segments, or orphaned 'done' markers. Investigation indicates gaps in client-visible session identifiers, insufficient per-session telemetry to correlate dropped chunks across proxies, and no lightweight server-side short-window replay for recent events. This ticket scopes a hybrid approach: enrich emitted SSE events with deterministic session metadata, create a short-lived in-memory session buffer for reconnect replay (<= 30s retention), and produce an SDK + ops playbook to merge partial outputs deterministically on the client. Goal is to eliminate customer-facing truncation and reduce manual incident escalations.
reproducible_steps: 1) Produce a long-running text generation request via Hosted API with SSE streaming enabled (example client: Node SDK streaming).
2) Allow stream to emit ~1k tokens, then simulate a client-side network interruption (SIGINT or proxy drop).
3) Reconnect within 10-30s and observe: client either resumes producing duplicate tokens, receives a final 'done' but misses trailing tokens, or receives fragmented events out-of-order.
4) Observe server-side logs correlating request_id but lacking session-level sequence metadata to match fragments from before and after the disconnect.
impact_summary: Multiple large customers have opened escalations (support tickets and CSM threads) where user-facing flows render incomplete chatbot replies or show duplicated tokens after reconnect. This causes high-severity UX regressions, increases churn risk, and forces manual incident interventions. Customer impact: high. Support time per incident: 3-8 hours on average.
proposed_solution: A) Add stable opaque session_id and monotonically increasing event_seq to every SSE event (text_chunk, partial_output, done). Include final_marker boolean for explicit finalization.
B) Implement short-window in-memory session buffer on the edge router (default retention 30s, configurable) that can replay missed events to reconnections authenticated with the same session_id.

C) Extend hosted SDKs (Node + Python) with a merge utility: client merges pre-disconnect fragments and post-reconnect fragments using event_seq + final_marker to produce a deterministic canonical stream for applications.
D) Add observability: new dashboards (per-session replay rate, replay success/failures, median reconnect latency), and structured logs (session_id, event_seq, replica_id).
E) Create customer-facing retry playbook and support runbook (detection heuristics, guided SDK patch, mitigation steps) to reduce escalations while server rollouts proceed.
F) Rate-limit replay requests per-customer to mitigate memory amplification and prevent abuse.
G) Provide rolling rollout behind feature flag with telemetry gates (replay success > 99% and <1% increase in memory at percentile P99) before GA.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SSE events emitted by hosted edge include session_id, event_seq, and final_marker in both streaming and non-streaming payloads.
2) Edge replay buffer can replay up to configured window (default 30s) for reconnects and is opt-in behind a runtime feature flag.
3) SDK merge utility published in Node and Python with docs and examples. SDKs pass integration tests that simulate midstream disconnect and reunification.
4) Observability dashboards show replay attempt rate and success rate. Telemetry gating integrated into rollout automation.
5) Support runbook and customer-facing playbook created and validated with Support and CSM teams. One pilot customer confirmed improved experience in staging.
6) No data leakage: session_id is opaque and contains no PII; security review completed and flagged as not requiring KMS changes.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Daniel Mercer: Initial investigation completed. Correlated three customer incidents to the same root cause: lack of session-level seq numbers. Captured pcap traces and server logs. Reference above incident notes.

2026-02-25 - Asha Patel: Proof-of-concept implemented for session_id + event_seq on the local dev router. Replay buffer prototype returning last 25s of events works for single-threaded tests. Observed ~0.8% memory overhead at low concurrency.

2026-03-01 - QA (Maya Lin): Integration tests created that simulate network blips; identified edge case where duplicate done markers from downstream proxy created finalization races. Added fix to idempotent final marker processing.
2026-03-04 - Security review (Omar Reyes): Reviewed session_id design. Confirmed using opaque random UUID v4 is acceptable; no PII in session metadata. Marked security_review_required = false.
2026-03-07 - Support (Leah Ortiz): Drafted customer retry playbook and two canned support responses. CSM team requested example that shows SDK merge snippet for web clients.

2026-03-10 - Eng Review (K. Huang): Code review requested changes: (1) expose config knob for retention window via runtime config service, (2) add soft memory cap per node. Asha acknowledged and will implement.

2026-03-12 - Release Lead (Priya Singh): Plan for staged rollout to non-prod on 2026-03-18, canary to 5% of traffic 2026-03-22, GA 2026-04-05 if telemetry gates pass. Added release tag runtime-1.20-canary.
2026-03-12 - Asha Patel: Updated PRs and documentation links posted. Starting cross-team QA with Support and SDK teams this week.
